question: What stool consistency pattern defines an episode of diarrhoea?

options.B: Single hard stool passed every three days
options.D: Three or more loose or liquid stools daily

explanation: Diarrhoea is clinically recognized by an increase in the frequency and liquidity of bowel movements, specifically passing three or more loose or liquid stools within a twenty-four-hour period. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h1)

question: What main body imbalance causes diarrhoea?

options.C: An imbalance between fluid absorption and secretion

explanation: Diarrhoea happens when the normal movement of fluid and electrolytes shifts, causing the intestines to secrete too much fluid or fail to absorb it properly. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which drug class slows down gut movement to allow more time for fluid absorption?
explanation: Motility inhibitors work on the smooth muscle of the gut to slow down peristalsis, keeping food and liquid in the intestines longer so the body can absorb more water. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do intestinal absorbents work in the digestive tract?

options.B: By completely paralyzing the enteric nervous system
options.C: By speeding up peristaltic movement waves
options.D: By binding toxins and excess fluid in the gut

explanation: Absorbents work by physically sticking to harmful toxins, bacteria, and excess water on their surface, neutralizing them inside the bowel. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h2)

question: Loperamide and diphenoxylate work by targeting receptors located in which part of the body?
explanation: These drugs act directly on opioid receptors found in the smooth muscle of the intestinal wall to slow down bowel movements. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why should motility inhibitors NOT be given to patients with a severe bacterial infection causing bloody diarrhoea?

options.A: They cause severe high blood pressure and stroke
options.B: They trap harmful germs and toxins inside the gut

explanation: Giving a motility inhibitor in these cases stops the body from getting rid of harmful germs, which traps them inside and can make the infection much worse. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which substance is a well-known example of an intestinal adsorbent?
explanation: Kaolin, often combined with pectin, is a classic adsorbent used to bind toxins and excess fluid in the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is a major risk when taking intestinal absorbents along with other oral drugs?

options.A: They can block the absorption of other oral medications
options.D: Rapid destruction of red blood cells

explanation: Because adsorbents stick to substances on their surface, they can also trap other oral medicines, stopping them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main action of racecadotril in the gut?

options.A: Reducing excessive water and electrolyte loss
options.D: Killing parasitic worms in the colon

explanation: Racecadotril stops the enzyme that breaks down natural body substances which normally reduce fluid and electrolyte loss into the gut. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why are antibiotics usually avoided in most cases of acute watery diarrhoea?

options.B: Most cases are caused by viruses and go away on their own
options.C: Germs instantly become immune to all drugs

explanation: Since most cases of acute diarrhoea are caused by viruses that clear up without treatment, routine antibiotics are unnecessary and only lead to drug resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: Oral rehydration therapy works best by using the intestinal transport of which pair of substances?
explanation: Sodium and glucose work together in the intestines to pull water into the bloodstream, which quickly rehydrates the body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is zinc supplementation given alongside oral rehydration salts to young children?

options.A: To act as a strong anti-diarrhoea drug
options.D: To shorten how long and how bad the illness is

explanation: Zinc helps repair the gut lining, strengthens the immune system, and helps children recover much faster from diarrhoea. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a sign of dehydration in an infant with severe diarrhoea?

options.B: Sunken soft spots on the head (fontanelles)

explanation: Depressed or sunken fontanelles on an infant's head are a clear sign of significant fluid loss and dehydration. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is keeping an accurate record of fluid intake and output vital during diarrhoea?

options.A: To check if the patient is gaining daily weight
options.B: To spot fluid shortages and guide replacement therapy
options.C: To calculate exact food calories needed
options.D: To find out the exact name of the germ causing the infection

explanation: Tracking fluid balance helps nurses see how much fluid is being lost so they can make sure the patient gets enough replacement fluids. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: How do most infectious diarrhoea germs spread from person to person?

options.A: Passed from mother to baby during pregnancy

explanation: Infectious diarrhoea mostly spreads when tiny, invisible amounts of stool pass from one person to another through contaminated hands, food, or water. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which public health step offers long-term protection against viral childhood diarrhoea?
explanation: Giving babies the rotavirus vaccine prevents the most common cause of severe, dehydrating viral stomach infections in young children. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h8)
